title: The month onion prices fell across India
summary: In February 2011, the median onion market moved -58.1% in a month, 4.8 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 4.8σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for onion, across 381 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: February 2011
scenes.caption: Onion prices across 381 markets that reported in both January 2011 and February 2011.

scenes.headline: Median move -58.1%
scenes.caption: The typical market's onion price fell 58.1% in one month. 100% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 4.8× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 4.8 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Maharashtra
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 37 reporting markets in Maharashtra had a median change of -63.8%.

scenes.headline: Tadepalligudem
scenes.caption: Tadepalligudem (Andhra Pradesh), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹3,700 → ₹1,275 per quintal (-65.5%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.
